summary: Ikuro Hattori specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Holding a Ph.D. from Pune University, he has been affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2003, 2026) and served as a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2026).

Ildikó Puskás (1942–2009) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied under János Harmatta from circa 1960 to 1966 and served on the faculty at Eötvös Loránd University from around 1968 to 2009.

Ilkka Pyysiäinen (born 1959) is a religious studies scholar who studied under René Gothóni (~1985–1993). He served as an Academy Research Fellow at the University of Helsinki in 1984 and as a visiting researcher at the University of Oxford.

Ilya Gershevitch (1914–2001) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Antonino Pagliaro, under Walter Bruno Henning, and at Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey, later lecturing at Cambridge (1948–1965).

Immanuel Bekker (1785–1871) worked in linguistics and history. After studying at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1803–1807), he spent his career at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1871) and taught Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler.
Imran Philip works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies under Kaustubh Mani Sengupta and held a Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Imre Bangha (born 1967) is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Visva-Bharati University (PhD 1998), later holding posts at Visva-Bharati (~1995–1999), Oxford/Wolfson College (around 2003), and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).

Imre Galambos (born 1967) specializes in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. Educated at ELTE, Nankai, and UC Berkeley (PhD 2002), he worked at the British Library (2002–2012), Cambridge (2012–2023), and Zhejiang University (~2023).

Imre Hamar (born 1967) studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under advisor Noritoshi Aramaki (~1994–1997). He became a professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006 and has served as a visiting professor at Otani University.
Imtiyaz Yusuf is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Temple University (1984–1990) and served as a professor at International Islamic University Malaysia in 2019.

In-gun Kang is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned degrees from the Jesuit School of Theology, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Heythrop College (attested 2012), where he studied under Michael Barnes.

Indira Viswanathan Peterson (born 1950) is an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She held posts at Columbia University and Mount Holyoke College (circa 1983–2019).

Ines Konczak-Nagel works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Her posts include the Berlin State Museums, Ryukoku University (2012), the Saxon Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and Leipzig University's Kuča-Projekt (attested 2026).

Ingmar Heise is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed an MA in Chinese Studies at Leiden University (graduated by 2005) and was a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol (attested 2012).

Ingo Strauch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin (-2000), where he held a post attested in 2008. In 2012, he became a professor at the University of Lausanne.
Inyoung Chung works in the field of Buddhist studies. Chung earned a PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner (attested 2008).

Ioan Mihălcescu (1874–1948) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Bucharest, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Leipzig (Ph.D. 1904), and became a Privatdozent at the University of Bucharest in 1904.

Ioan Petru Culianu (1950–1991) was a religious studies scholar and historian. He studied at Bucharest, Università Cattolica, Paris-Sorbonne, and under Mircea Eliade. He held posts at the University of Groningen (1976–1986) and University of Chicago Divinity School (1986–1991).

Iona Macgregor works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Hamburg, where she also served as a project research associate (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin, attested 2026).
Ippei Okamoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at Toyo University (attested 2014) and served as a visiting research fellow at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
